=== Original census and working father, 23 October 2026 ===

The original 1851 Glenleslie household 21 return records John Glasgow as 100, Rose as 80, and 1791 for both. Its marriage heading asks “In what Year Married, or in what Years if more than once?” The detailed transcription’s first-marriage field is therefore an editorial description, not the literal question on this return. Only 1791 is entered: an earlier union is not documented, and the request for multiple years means its absence still weighs against a straightforward earlier-marriage explanation. The original also calls the forty-year-old John a nephew and gives his occupation as vagrant; the 1839 marriage belongs to him. The mortality table explicitly calls Andrew Glasgow, a thirty-year-old linen weaver who died of consumption in winter 1848, a son of the head. It does not name Andrew’s mother.

Select John Glasgow-1022 as the possible working father of the Glenleslie Robert represented by Glasgow-1367, at 38% subjective confidence. The original makes their reported age difference 28 years (100 versus 72), a comfortable father–son interval. They were Antrim-born Glasgow farmers in Glenleslie households 21 and 23, separated by the Hamill household. This is a specific nearby older family, and John is the best identified local father comparison already retained in the research. Reading the original marriage question removes the previous overstatement that it expressly records a first marriage in 1791. The combined generation and neighbouring-family argument is sufficient to select a weak working model rather than leave this preferred named comparison outside the tree; it is not a parent statement.

38% assesses the complete John-to-Robert profile hypothesis, not the certainty of reading the census. Robert’s census-implied birth about 1778–1779 precedes the sole reported marriage year by roughly twelve years. An earlier union, nonmarital fatherhood or a reporting error would still be needed, and none is established. The original asks for multiple marriage years, so omission of an earlier year remains a real limitation. John’s exceptional age may be inaccurate. An uncle, cousin, other collateral relative or unrepresented father remains possible; the older Alexander comparison is not excluded. Rose’s reported age does not fit her as Robert’s mother, and no mother or earlier wife is assigned. The selection concerns the 1851 Glenleslie man only: it does not identify him with the Lisnagaver tithe occupier, validate every attached child, or prove a Y-DNA pedigree. Hugh-3956’s 74% brother hypothesis includes a separate identity uncertainty and is not automatically assigned this father; his estimated earlier generation also needs its own chronology test. The inherited Unknown Glasgow-3905 is preserved as an uncertain alternative with no invented percentage. No live WikiTree family field is changed.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-3959]] is assessed at 27% (uncertain). The Ballyboggy John active in 1740 is a real earlier Antrim adult and could father the Glenleslie John born about 1751. The existing local pedigree offers a coherent older generation, but no shared holding or named-relative source bridges these men.

Uncertain27%; the older man’s c 1705 birth is an estimate, not an independently known age. The 1851 Glenleslie household proves later relatives, not this father.

=== Glenleslie father comparison ===

[[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] of Glenleslie is an uncertain father candidate, assessed at 18%, for the Glenleslie [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]]. Their reported ages of 99 and 72 in 1851 give a plausible father–son generation, and both were Antrim-born farmers in houses 21 and 23. The census transcription, however, gives John’s first marriage as 1791, about twelve years after Robert’s estimated birth. Earlier fatherhood would require nonmarital fatherhood or an error or omission in the return; no earlier wife or union is established. Collateral kinship and another father remain more likely overall. Neither census entry states their relationship.<ref>[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf 1851 Irish Census Returns, detailed comma-delimited transcription], field definitions PDF p. 1 (field 17, first-marriage year), Glenleslie households 21–23 PDF p. 103. John’s original return has not been newly inspected. The original of Robert’s household is National Archives of Ireland, [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/census-record/#id=31234&census_year=1851 Glenleslie household 23].</ref>

This unselected hypothesis concerns the Glenleslie census man. It does not identify the Lisnagaver tithe occupier, supply a mother or establish the wider pedigree.
